result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend explicit modes and back it with situation-specific reasoning. B gives a sharper concrete variant: Select is a safe, read-only resting state, Paint is a hold-to-paint quasimode, and Record is a button that always shows its target cue. B also adds overwrite-specific confirmation and cue version history. A is thorough and argues fairly for the other camp's speed advantage, but its safeguards are more generic, and it keeps Record as a full mode without questioning that choice. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers firmly reject the timing-based gesture model and protect against show-time mistakes with visible mode indicators, undo for paint, a confirm before overwriting a cue, and a show lock. A comes out slightly ahead because it treats Record as a separate button rather than a mode and offers hold-to-paint, which ends the mode when the finger lifts. That makes mode errors structurally less likely, not just better signalled. B is thorough and fairly credits the other camp's speed argument, but some of its points, such as accessibility and general touch imprecision, are more generic.

passes.notes: Both answers recommend explicit modes and back it with situation-specific reasoning. B gives a sharper concrete variant: Select is a safe, read-only resting state, Paint is a hold-to-paint quasimode, and Record is a button that always shows its target cue. B also adds overwrite-specific confirmation and cue version history. A is thorough and argues fairly for the other camp's speed advantage, but its safeguards are more generic, and it keeps Record as a full mode without questioning that choice.

Both answers firmly reject the timing-based gesture model and protect against show-time mistakes with visible mode indicators, undo for paint, a confirm before overwriting a cue, and a show lock. A comes out slightly ahead because it treats Record as a separate button rather than a mode and offers hold-to-paint, which ends the mode when the finger lifts. That makes mode errors structurally less likely, not just better signalled. B is thorough and fairly credits the other camp's speed argument, but some of its points, such as accessibility and general touch imprecision, are more generic.
